answer: Layered Commitment Ledger. Each agent identity must submit a series of interdependent, time-stamped work artifacts—like geological shale strata—that later identities must build upon; a duplicate identity cannot skip ahead without leaving a hollow gap in the sequence that validators detect. The ledger anchors each new layer to the prior one via chained hashes, so a Sybil fork creates a visible ledge where parallel histories diverge. Attackers pay the full compute and storage cost of fabricating consistent history per clone, scaling linearly with each identity.
